title: True Scale
heading: BadCode Shorts ▲ True Scale

beats.name: 1. Tiebreaker
beats.blurb: Pub quiz night. Mic feedback. The quizmaster: 'Tiebreaker! Nearest wins the meat raffle. How many homes in England have been empty six months or more?'

beats.name: 2. The guesses
beats.blurb: Quick cuts: confident guesses scribbled and shouted ('Ten grand.' 'Fifty thousand, tops.'). Bob, a team of one in the corner, writes without hesitating.

beats.name: 3. The answer
beats.blurb: 'Three hundred and three thousand. Not counting two hundred and sixty-seven thousand second homes.' Groans. 'Nearest... table nine. Bob.'

beats.name: 4. How'd you know?
beats.blurb: The whole pub turns to look at Bob for the first time; rucksack and sleeping mat already on. 'How'd you know that?' Bob: Jack's line.

beats.name: 5. The prize
beats.blurb: Bob takes the meat raffle, has nowhere to cook it, hands it on, walks out into the rain. Quizmaster: '...Right. Picture round.'

moodboard_intro: Round 1 (clean room, Jack 2026-11-16: "do the uk stats, in intresting varied ways as stills"): four sealed writers, one per beat, fresh web research, nothing from the repo, three different ideas each. A one household (model figures on an endless table; a B&B room from the ceiling; a family's belongings in one car-park bay) · B 134,210 (a car park of suitcases; a B&B key board that never ends; a pin map of England) · C 303,185 empty homes (an aerial of dark terraces; a lettings office wall of keys; a model on a community-hall table) · D 267,894 second homes (a diorama where the fourth block lights up; a seaside town lit for nobody; a wall of key safes). Keys turned up in three beats: it could be a thread through the film. Numbers: official, checked (numbers.md). Vote This / Maybe / No per still and note any beat.
